neutral_facts.value: The victim was returning home on a bicycle when he was stopped by an individual who poured petrol over him and set him on fire. The victim ran away but was surrounded by several individuals who encouraged others to beat and burn him. The victim was unable to escape and was eventually found burned and injured. A witness who was present at the scene reported that the victim was set on fire and that others were involved in surrounding him and encouraging the attack. The post-mortem report confirmed severe burns and an incised wound on the victim's back, supporting the account of the witness. The prosecution relied on the witness's testimony and the post-mortem findings to establish the involvement of the accused in the attack.

key_evidence_accepted.value: The Supreme Court accepted the dying declarations (statements Ext. P-20 and P-17) and the testimony of the eye witness PW13 as key evidence, which consistently named the respondents and described their role in surrounding the deceased and preventing his escape.

quotes.text: Statement Ext. P-20 leading to the registration of crime as well as statement Ext. P-17 recorded by the Executive Magistrate are dying declarations by the victim-deceased. Both these statements are consistent and name the respondents and state the role played by them in surrounding the deceased and giving cries that he be beaten and should not be left.

witness_credibility.value: The court assessed the main witnesses, including PW13, as credible eye witnesses whose testimony was corroborated by the post-mortem report, indicating their presence and active participation in the crime.

quotes.text: The presence of said PW13 was completely established. He was eye witness to the occurrence. In the light of the eye witness account and the post mortem report, it is quite clear that the respondents were present when the deceased was burning alive.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the deceased was caught by the accused, petrol was poured over him, and fire was lit. The deceased ran, was surrounded by the respondents, and attacked with a sword and burning tyre. The trial court convicted all the accused, and the High Court's acquittal was challenged.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the role of the respondents in the commission of the crime was clearly established by the dying declaration and eye witness testimony, indicating their active participation and intent.

quotes.text: Role of respondents in the commission of crime was clearly made out from the dying declaration as well as testimony of the eye witness

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the respondents were found to have participated in the crime, acted in concert, and ensured the deceased could not escape, thereby fulfilling the elements of the offence under Section 302 read with Section 149 of the Penal Code.
